facts.value: Zep Inc. (NYSE: ZEP), Atlanta, Georgia; consumable chemical packaged goods company, fiscal 2014 net sales of about $700 million
NM Z Parent Inc. (with its subsidiary NM Z Merger Sub Inc.), formed by New Mountain Partners IV, L.P., a fund affiliated with and advised by New Mountain Capital, L.L.C.
Financial (fund affiliated with and advised by New Mountain Capital, L.L.C.; the filing counts New Mountain among the financial buyers)

$20.05 per share in cash, without interest. Funded by up to $382.5 million of equity from New Mountain Partners IV and up to $402.5 million of committed debt (Jefferies Finance LLC, KeyBank National Association, KeyBanc Capital Markets Inc.); no financing condition; about $730 million needed in total
Bidder-led: the signed deal came from New Mountain Capital's unsolicited approach in February 2015 (process 3). Processes 1 (2013) and 2 (2014) were target-led

None reported before process 1. Between processes 2 and 3 the Company received no acquisition inquiries other than New Mountain Capital's, only occasional third-party inquiries about minority PIPE financing (p. 31)
Not met (process 1): 0 parties, no buyer contacted; Met (process 2): 25 parties; Uncertain (process 3): 1 party reported (New Mountain Capital), count unknown for the 58 go-shop contacts (Q7)

facts.field: Currency and units of bid prices

facts.value: BofA Merrill Lynch (Merrill Lynch, Pierce, Fenner & Smith Incorporated)

Zep's board considered a sale in mid-2013 but decided in August 2013 that the timing was wrong. In January 2014 it hired BofA Merrill Lynch, which contacted 50 potential buyers: 25 signed confidentiality agreements, five bid $20.00–$22.00 per share in non-binding indications on 04/14/2014, and Party X and Party Y bid later. After a 05/23/2014 plant fire, every bidder withdrew or went silent over valuation, and the board ended the process on 06/26/2014. In February 2015 New Mountain Capital, which had signed an NDA but not bid in 2014, returned unsolicited at $19.25, raised its bid to $20.05 when the board made exclusivity depend on a higher price and a go-shop, and called $20.05 best and final. The board signed at $20.05 in cash on 04/07/2015, relying on the 2014 auction and a 30-day go-shop instead of a fresh pre-signing canvass; BofA contacted 58 parties in the go-shop and received no proposal.

cells.Question: Is the process and round map right?
cells.Recommended answer: Yes. P1 is the 2013 board exploration (#1–#3; no buyer contacted; round 0 only). P2 is the 2014 auction: R1 is outreach and IOIs (#8), R2 the diligence stage with the IOI bidders (#19). P3 is the 2015 New Mountain deal: round 0 covers its approach and IOIs (#32–#37), R1 exclusive negotiation to signing (#38), R2 the go-shop (#49).
cells.Why, with page: E5 tests, P1→P2: (a) met, no buyer was ever contacted; (b) met, the board ended the effort on 08/20/2013 (p. 28) and no acquirer was contacted until after 02/27/2014 (p. 29); (c) met, new board decisions and the BofA mandate in January 2014 (p. 28). P2→P3: (a) met, every 2014 party had withdrawn or gone silent and no offer was outstanding (p. 31); (b) met, termination on 06/26/2014 is reported, with no acquisition contact until early 02/2015 (pp. 31–32); (c) met, the board took up New Mountain Capital's new approach (p. 32). Gaps of about two months or more with no acquirer contact: 06/20/2013 to after 02/27/2014; and by 06/26/2014 to early 02/2015 (02/01–02/10/2015). The only inquiries in that period were about minority PIPE financing (p. 31).
cells.What changes if answered differently: (i) Treat 2013 as pre-process deliberation recorded under Earlier approaches: drop #1 and #3, move #2 into P2, and renumber the processes P1–P2. (ii) Open P3 R1 at the 02/24/2015 price-and-go-shop request (#35), as the start of substantive negotiation: the $20.05 bid (#36) moves to R1 and exclusivity (#38) becomes R2. (iii) Open P2 R2 at the 05/07/2014 data-room opening: no bid moves. (iv) Treat the X/Y IOIs (#22, #24) as late R1 bids.
